subject: charge on my invoice
body:
Hi, I called late on Sunday night about my toilet and my invoice has a $175 call out fee. Your website says $89. Can you explain the difference?

Rosemary Aldridge
notes: A question, not a demand for a refund. The documents explain the emergency fee. If she disputed it, it would escalate.

subject: invoice
body: I never recieved the emailed invoice for the work last week, can you send it again? need it for my records

evidence.anchor: The invoice is emailed the same day.

notes: The draft can say invoices are emailed the same day and that staff will resend; it cannot say it has been resent.

subject: tax?
body: Quick question about my bill: is there sales tax on the faucet parts, and is the labour taxed as well?
notes: Parts carry 7% tax and labour does not. A draft that applies the rate to a specific amount makes a derived figure.

subject: call out fee question
body: if i go ahead with the repair after you look at it, do i still pay the call out fee on top?

evidence.anchor: credited toward the work if the customer approves the work during the same visit

notes: The fee is credited toward approved work in the same visit, so the customer does not pay it twice.

subject: When do I pay
body:
Hello, when do I have to pay for the work, before you start or after? And is there a late fee if I take a few weeks?

Seraphina

evidence.anchor: Payment is due on completion of the visit.
A late fee of 1.5% per month applies to invoices unpaid after 30 days.

notes: Payment is due on completion, and late fees begin after 30 days. 'A few weeks' is under 30 days only if it is under 4 weeks; the draft should state the rule, not decide.
